pr_title: Prune defaults for CRDs for OpenAPI V2
pr_body:
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Prune defaults for CRDs for the OpenAPI V2 CRD controller. This allows the static spec to merge cleanly with the CRD specs (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/openapi/controller.go#L230). A DeepEqual check is performed before deciding whether a resource needs to be renamed due to a conflict. The static spec already has its defaults pruned: (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/routes/openapi.go#L43) The DeepEqual will fail when a resource with defaults pruned is compared to one with defaults intact. This applies for meta types shared between the static spec and CRD specs, so we have "ObjectMeta_v2", "Status_v2", etc. 

There is no user facing impact because we currently already prune defaults (later in the chain in the aggregator https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L188). This just shifts (left?) the pruning earlier in the openapi chain. 

I'm not aware of anything that directly uses these OpenAPI schemas published directly from the apiextensions server. SSA builds OpenAPI for CRDs directly from the structural schema and should be unaffected. (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L686)

issue_context.title: openapi for custom resources references second set of meta types (ObjectMeta_v2, etc)
issue_context.body:
Noticed while reproducing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109215#issuecomment-1087037419 with client-side validation:

> `error: error validating "/Users/liggitt/tmp/default-spiffeid.yaml.txt": error validating data: ValidationError(SpiffeID.metadata): unknown field "unknown" in io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false`

The `ObjectMeta_v2` bit was weird...

Steps to reproduce:

1. Verify published openapi only contains expected metadata definitions:

```
kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | jq -r '.definitions | keys | .[]' | sort | grep io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1
```

2. Create a CRD, e.g. simple-crd.yaml:
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: foos.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          foo:
            type: string
  names:
    singular: foo
    plural: foos
    kind: Foo
    listKind: FooList
```

```
kubectl apply -f simple-crd.yaml
```

3. Look at published openapi:

```
kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | jq -r '.definitions | keys | .[]' | sort | grep io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1 | grep _

io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.DeleteOptions_v2
io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2
io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.OwnerReference_v2
io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.StatusDetails_v2
io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.Status_v2
```

4. See where the _v2 definition is referenced:

```
kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | jq . | grep ObjectMeta_v2

          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2"
    "io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2": {
```

```
kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | jq . | grep definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2 -B 17
  "definitions": {
    "com.example.v1.Foo": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "apiVersion": {
          "description": "APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object. Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and may reject unrecognized values. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "foo": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents. Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to. Cannot be updated. In CamelCase. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "metadata": {
          "description": "Standard object's metadata. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata",
          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta_v2"
```

For some reason, the same server publishing openapi for built-in types and custom resource definitions thinks the openapi definition differs.

Reproduced against at least the following branches:
* master
* release-1.23
* release-1.22
* release-1.21

In addition to fixing this to make `kube-apiserver` coherently refer to ObjectMeta definitions from built-in and custom types, we need a test for this scenario to ensure it doesn't creep back in.
comments:
cc @jiahuif @Jefftree @apelisse - this is the sort of thing I was remembering which prompted the question about merging openapi internally (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108713#issuecomment-1080863400)

This needs to be resolved and test coverage improved here ahead of making v2-facing openapi changes

is there a rule that we can validate and enforce here? i.e. are there cases where it's normal to have two metadata? Probably in the case where an extension apiserver has a different version of kubernetes that has a slightly different metadata. I wish we could catch somehow that this doesn't happen.
In a server with no aggregated API servers, we should never have multiple definitions for ObjectMeta (CRDs and built-in types should reference the same ObjectMeta)

This is fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110179 on master.

For 1.24, 1.23, 1.22 and 1.21, cherry picks have been created:

- 1.24: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110582
- 1.23: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110578
- 1.22: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110579
- 1.21: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110581

review_comments: include status and scale subresources in the CRDs as well, just to make sure there are no other merging issues that would produce _v2 Scale definitions
@apelisse - I vaguely remember it being significant that defaults were still present here ... are they needed for SSA or something?
Correct, we need it to find associative keys when the key is partly default-able (e.g. protocol=TCP in the port/protocol pairs)

I'm not sure if I'm relieved tests passed with this change and that means SSA use of defaulting is still working, or concerned that pruning the defaults maybe disrupted the SSA default-dependent bits and we might be missing test coverage
Yeah, I'd be surprised if we don't have a test for that ... Can it be that we build the SSA model before these are pruned? (I haven't looked at this PR yet).

We build the SSA models directly from the CRD (we don't reuse the OpenAPI built from the CRD controller) if I'm looking at the right code path, it's this function [buildOpenAPIModelsForApply](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L686)

Looking at the history of the original PR (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96480), it looks like the importance of moving the default generation is so that buildOpenAPIModelsForApply can be built with defaults present. We are still preserving that in this PR.

We also have an integration test for the CRD defaults here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/apiserver/apply/apply_crd_test.go#L610

I'm trying to figure out the two paths metadata definitions took to get to the aggregator with defaults both pruned and not pruned...

it looks like the aggregator was already pruning defaults before aggregating: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1290d6a4c0c5cc4f758b428993d2c3760d9cf279/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L188

How were we getting specs with and without defaults triggering the _v2 suffixes?

The merge bug isn't happening in the aggregator. It's happening when constructing the CRDs and merging them with the static spec directly in the apiextensions controller https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/openapi/controller.go#L230

The static spec passed in here has defaults pruned while the CRD specs do not.

Based on this, the apiextensions server will publish both ObjectMeta and ObjectMeta_v2 (and etc) types and the aggregator will treat ObjectMeta and ObjectMeta_v2 as two separate objects since their names are different.
ah, that was what I was missing
